Articles I-IX.title: Codex of the Fallen Star
Articles I-IX.message:
### Article I. Loyalty to the Order Above All

The Order stands above self, coin, and clan. All personal alliances, factions, and pursuits are secondary to the will and interests of the Order. Betrayal of the Order is the gravest offense and is judged by the Council or the Emperors.

### Article II. Authority, Command, and the Chain of Obedience

Authority flows downward through the chain of command. Responsibility and accountability flow upward. The Council interprets the will of the Emperors and resolves disputes of authority. Bypassing the chain of command without just cause invites censure.

### Article III. The Duty of Mentorship and Training

Each Knight may take up to two Pages under their guidance and prepare them for service as Squires and eventual Knighthood. Those entrusted with mentorship are expected to lead, train, and uphold standards. Failure to fulfill these duties may result in reassignment or the loss of mentorship privileges.

### Article IV. The Keeping of Records and Deeds

All sanctioned operations, whether conducted as Quests or Crusades as defined in Appendix I, must be recorded in full, including participants, objectives, outcomes, spoils, and individual contributions. Records exist to ensure fairness, accountability, and the proper recognition of service. Knowingly falsifying records is a severe offense and is investigated by Chancellors and judged by the Council.

### Article V. Conduct, Discipline, and Honor

Members of the Order are expected to act with discipline, restraint, and respect for the Codex. Unjust harm toward non-combatants, allies, or neutral parties is forbidden unless explicitly sanctioned. Disputes within the Order are to be addressed through proper channels and not aired publicly.

### Article VI. Relics, Seals, and Property of the Order

All relics, banners, seals, and artifacts are the property of the Order. No such item may be claimed, sold, removed, or defiled without formal decree. Violations of this article are judged before the Council.

### Article VII. Judgment, Trials, and Enforcement of the Codex

Chancellors serve as investigators and enforcers of the Codex, gathering evidence and carrying out judgments. The Council rules on major violations and matters of high consequence. The Emperors hold final authority and may issue binding decrees.

Minor violations may be resolved by presiding officers. Intermediate breaches are reviewed by a Justicar and escalated when required. High crimes such as treason, falsification of records, or relic theft are judged by the Council, subject to Emperor authority.

### Article VIII. Spoils, Tithes, and Contribution

All spoils gained through sanctioned operations must be recorded in the appropriate quest or crusade record. Distribution of spoils and rewards is determined by documented contribution and service to the Order.

The Order recognizes an internal currency of copper, silver, and gold as a measure of service, time, and contribution. This currency is issued, recorded, and regulated by the Order and may be used for compensation, allocation of spoils, and other sanctioned purposes.

Currency issuance, reward allocation, and contribution recognition may vary between Quests and Crusades in accordance with their scale and purpose, as defined in Appendix I.

A tithe of ten percent is claimed by the Order prior to distribution to fund logistics, relic upkeep, and crusades. Misrepresentation, concealment, or manipulation of spoils or currency is considered a serious violation of the Codex.

### Article IX. Secrecy, Knowledge, and Classified Matters

Operational plans, relic locations, and Council decrees are considered restricted unless formally authorized. The careless or deliberate disclosure of protected information is a major violation and is reviewed by the Council.

### Article X. Emergency Authority in Times of Crisis

During moments of grave threat, Knights and those above them may act beyond normal permissions to preserve life, relics, or operational integrity. This authority may apply to both Quests and Crusades when circumstances demand immediate action. All such actions must be recorded and are subject to review once the crisis has passed.

### Article XI. Advancement, Merit, and Worthiness

Advancement within the Order is earned through documented contribution, demonstrated merit, and proven capability. Trials of skill, leadership, doctrine, or service may be required. Advancement granted without merit is corruption and is punishable by demotion.

### Article XII. Authority of the Codex and the Enduring Star

This Codex reflects the will of the Fallen Star and governs all who serve beneath its light. The Primarchs' decree stands above all other law. Amendments to the Codex require the approval of the Primarch or the unanimous consent of the Council of Ascension.

### Appendix I. Quests and Crusades

The Order recognizes two sanctioned forms of organized action: Quests and Crusades. Both serve the Order and are governed by the Codex, but they differ in scale, intent, and authority.

### Quests

A Quest is an operational action undertaken in response to immediate needs, opportunities, or circumstances.

• Quests are typically impromptu or lightly planned.
• Quests typically involve a small to moderate number of members.
• Objectives are practical, short-term, or exploratory in nature.
•Quests may be initiated by Knights or higher authority when circumstances require action. • The sole exception is a Squire acting under the direct supervision of a Knight.
• Outcomes, spoils, and contributions must be recorded in the quest record.
• Quests form the foundation of day-to-day service within the Order.

### Crusades

A Crusade is a large-scale, deliberate operation undertaken in pursuit of a major objective aligned with the long-term interests of the Order.

• Crusades are planned in advance and formally sanctioned.
• Crusades involve a broad assembly of members, often across multiple ranks, Paths, or Chapters.
• Objectives are strategic, ceremonial, territorial, or pivotal to the Order’s direction.
• Crusades are typically initiated or approved by senior leadership.
• Participation, time committed, and outcomes are formally recorded and reviewed.
• Crusades represent moments of collective effort and unified purpose.

### Distinction and Application

• Quests address immediate needs and routine operations.
• Crusades advance the long-term vision and strategic objectives of the Order.

Both Quests and Crusades are subject to the authority, recordkeeping requirements, currency systems, and disciplinary standards established by the Codex of the Fallen Star.

Time in Service and Merit Consid.message:
### Time in Service and Merit Consideration

Minimum time-in-service requirements listed for each rank represent the standard progression path within the Order.

Demonstrated merit through active participation may offset time-based requirements. Merit is measured through documented Quests and Crusades, reputation earned within the community, and sustained contribution to the Order.

When a member’s reputation, service record, and leadership conduct clearly exceed the expectations of their current rank, advancement may be considered prior to the minimum time requirement.

All time waivers:
• Require review by the Council for the rank in question
• Must be supported by documented quest and crusade records
• May not bypass eligibility, authority, or oath requirements

** Time-in-service may not be waived for disciplinary reasons or in cases of incomplete Codex understanding.**

The Treasury of the Order.title: The Treasury of the Order
The Treasury of the Order.message:
The Treasury of the Order exists to ensure that those who serve are properly rewarded for their time, loyalty, and contribution to the quest. Members may claim their earned payment through the bank system once their pay has been granted.

To access the Treasury, members must type the following command in any text channel:

**/bank**

Once the bank menu appears, select **View Pay**, then choose **Collect Pay** to receive any available payment.

Members may also access the shop to purchase available items. To open the shop, members must type the following command in any text channel:

**/shop**

Once the shop menu appears, members may review the available items and complete any purchases they are eligible to make.

All members are expected to claim only what has been rightfully earned and purchase only through the proper channels. The Treasury stands as a record of service, trust, and contribution within the Order. Those who labor in the name of the Fallen Star shall be compensated, and those who abuse the Treasury shall answer before the Council.
